title: Add RAG authoring presets and VSCode linting plugin for faster local prototyping
author: Sophie Lin
release_notes: Adds a VSCode extension and a set of opinionated RAG authoring presets for local prototyping. Includes a short quickstart, sample presets for streaming vs batch, and built-in lint rules to catch common tool-calling mistakes. No breaking API changes.
body: Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a low-friction way to author and iterate on RAG agent tool-calling flows locally without spinning up the full infra or writing lots of boilerplate. This change adds an editor-integrated workflow (VSCode extension) plus a set of opt-in authoring presets and lint rules designed to surface common prompt/tool mismatches early in development. Summary of changes: 1) new example 'vscode-rag-authoring' extension that provides commands: 'RAG: Start Local Sandbox', 'RAG: Run Step', 'RAG: Replay Session' and an inline lint panel with rules for malformed tool schemas and mismatched tool-call signatures; 2) presets under redwood-quickstarts/rag-presets/ — streaming-min-latency, batch-cost-optimized, and dev-prototyping which wire up example prompts, a lightweight local vector store mock, and eval harness snippets; 3) docs and quickstart page updates in redwood-examples/docs/rag-authoring-presets.md with screenshots and a troubleshooting section; 4) test harness updates (playwright smoke + unit tests) and CI integration. Implementation notes: - The VSCode extension is implemented as a thin shim that talks to the existing local sandbox runner in examples/sandbox via HTTP on a random ephemeral port. It intentionally avoids shipping heavy native dependencies; the local runner remains the single source of truth for sandbox behavior. - Lint rules are small JSON-schema-based checks with a few JS helper rules (tool-signature checks, required-example prompts, detection of immediate-looping action patterns). They run in the extension and as a CLI check (npm run rag-lint). - Presets are authored as plain YAML files and include a small metadata block that the extension reads to populate the preset picker. Checklist: - [x] VSCode extension scaffolding and commands - [x] Local sandbox runner updates and auth shim - [x] Three presets with example prompts - [x] Lint rule set + CLI runner - [x] Quickstart doc and screenshots - [x] Unit tests for lint rules and runner - [x] E2E smoke via Playwright Notes on compatibility and rollout: - No changes to public Redwood API surfaces. Customers using Hosted/Dedicated/Private are unaffected. - The presets are examples only and opt-in; they do not change runtime defaults. - To reduce CI noise, the extension build is gated behind a lightweight smoke job; full extension packaging is done in a separate release pipeline. How to try locally: 1) git checkout HEAD && cd redwood-examples/vscode-rag-authoring 2) npm ci && npm run start:dev 3) Open VSCode (Developer: Install Extension from VSIX) and install the generated VSIX to get the quick commands, or use the included devcontainer. 4) Run 'RAG: Start Local Sandbox' then 'RAG: Run Step' to execute a single tool call against the local mock. Testing and CI: Unit tests for lint rules added under tests/lint/; Playwright scenario exercises the 'Run Step' command and asserts telemetry and output snapshots. See ci_checks for the run-by-run summary. Related: ENG-1412 (authoring UX improvements), PM-873 (quickstart adoption goal).
